\begin{theorem}[Code Segment After Two Expressions]
\lean{Light.Compiler.codeAt_after_pair}
\label{Light.Compiler.codeAt_after_pair}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.compileExpr, Light.Compiler.length_compileExpr, Light.Expr.size, WordRAM.CodeAt, WordRAM.CodeAt.cast_pos, WordRAM.CodeAt.right}
\difficulty{3}
Let $code$ be a finite instruction list, $pos$ a natural-number position, $a,b$
expressions, and $rest$ an instruction list. If the concatenation of the compiled code
for $a$ at temporary index $0$, the compiled code for $b$ at temporary index $1$, and
$rest$ is a prefix of the code beginning at $pos$, then $rest$ is a prefix of the code
beginning at $pos+\mathrm{size}(a)+\mathrm{size}(b)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of two expressions]
\lean{Light.Compiler.steps_pair}
\label{Light.Compiler.steps_pair}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.Framed, Light.Compiler.Framed.same, Light.Compiler.Scratch, Light.Compiler.cT, Light.Compiler.compileExpr, Light.Compiler.effects_compileExpr_of_width, Light.Compiler.length_compileExpr, Light.Compiler.straight_compileExpr, Light.Compiler.temps_subset_scratch, Light.Expr.Safe, Light.Expr.size, Light.Expr.val, Light.Expr.width, WordRAM.AgreeOutside, WordRAM.AgreeOutside.mono, WordRAM.AgreeOutside.read, WordRAM.AgreeOutside.trans, WordRAM.CodeAt, WordRAM.CodeAt.left, WordRAM.Steps, WordRAM.effects_append, WordRAM.steps_straight, WordRAM.wd}
\difficulty{5}
Let $Z$ be admissible compiler size data of word size $W$, with state $\sigma$
represented in a stack frame at depth $q$ by memory $m$, where $1\le q$ and $q+F\le Q$.
Suppose the code at $\mathrm{pos}$ begins with the compiled code for expressions $a$ and
$b$ using temporary slots $0$ and $1$, respectively; both expressions have width at most
$F$ and are safe under the limits and state $\sigma$. Then some memory $m'$ is reached
after $a$'s size plus $b$'s size machine steps, at program counter
$\mathrm{pos}+a.\mathrm{size}+b.\mathrm{size}$, with temporary slots $0$ and $1$
containing the words encoding the respective values of $a$ and $b$ in $\sigma$. The
memories agree outside the scratch-address set for $F$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Bounded decision by a program]
\lean{Light.Compiler.Decides}
\label{Light.Compiler.Decides}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.Scratch, WordRAM.AgreeOutside, WordRAM.Instr, WordRAM.Steps}
Let $C$ be a list of word-RAM instructions, and let $F$, $p_0$, $s$, and $\ell$ be
natural numbers, $m$ an integer-addressed memory of $W$-bit words, and $P$ a
proposition. The program decides $P$ if there exist a final memory $m'$ and a natural
number $n\le s$ such that $m$ and $m'$ agree outside the scratch locations for $F$, and:
if $P$ holds, the program takes exactly $n$ steps from position $p_0$ with memory $m$ to
position $p_0+s$ with memory $m'$; if $P$ fails, it takes exactly $n$ steps from that
same initial configuration to position $\ell$ with memory $m'$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Execution When a Predicate Holds]
\lean{Light.Compiler.Decides.of_holds}
\label{Light.Compiler.Decides.of_holds}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.Decides, Light.Compiler.Scratch, WordRAM.AgreeOutside, WordRAM.Steps}
\difficulty{1}
Let $W,F,\mathrm{pos},\mathrm{size},l\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{code}$ be a program
for a word RAM with $W$-bit words, let $m$ be its initial memory, and let $p$ be a
proposition. Suppose there exist a memory $m'$ and a number $n\le\mathrm{size}$ such
that $m'$ agrees with $m$ at every address outside the scratch set, and the program runs
for $n$ steps from program position $\mathrm{pos}$ and memory $m'$ whenever $p$ holds,
reaching position $\mathrm{pos}+\mathrm{size}$. If $p$ holds, then there exist such an
$m'$ and $n\le\mathrm{size}$, with the same agreement outside the scratch set, for which
the program runs from position $\mathrm{pos}$ and memory $m$ for $n$ steps to position
$\mathrm{pos}+\mathrm{size}$. Here the scratch set consists of addresses
$-21,-15,-17,-19,-13$ and addresses $-(23+4j)$ for integers $j$ with $0\le j\le 2F$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Execution When a Predicate Fails]
\lean{Light.Compiler.Decides.of_fails}
\label{Light.Compiler.Decides.of_fails}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.Decides, Light.Compiler.Scratch, WordRAM.AgreeOutside, WordRAM.Steps}
\difficulty{1}
Let $W,F,\mathrm{pos},\mathrm{size},l\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{code}$ be a program
for a word RAM with $W$-bit words, let $m$ be its initial memory, and let $p$ be a
proposition. Suppose there exist a memory $m'$ and a number $n\le\mathrm{size}$ such
that $m'$ agrees with $m$ at every address outside the scratch set, and the program runs
for $n$ steps from program position $\mathrm{pos}$ and memory $m'$ whenever $p$ holds,
reaching position $\mathrm{pos}+\mathrm{size}$. If $p$ is false, then there exist such
an $m'$ and $n\le\mathrm{size}$, with the same agreement outside the scratch set, for
which the program runs from position $\mathrm{pos}$ and memory $m$ for $n$ steps to
position $l$. Here the scratch set consists of addresses $-21,-15,-17,-19,-13$ and
addresses $-(23+4j)$ for integers $j$ with $0\le j\le 2F$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Range bounds for bounded differences]
\lean{Light.Compiler.inRange_sub}
\label{Light.Compiler.inRange_sub}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.Sizes, WordRAM.InRange}
\difficulty{4}
Let $W$ be a natural number and let $Z$ be a size specification for word width $W$. If
$x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$ satisfy $|x|\le Z$'s word limit and $|y|\le Z$'s word limit, then
both $x-y$ and $x-y-1$ satisfy $-2^W\le 2v<2^W$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Compiled strict inequality test]
\lean{Light.Compiler.decides_lt}
\label{Light.Compiler.decides_lt}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.Decides, Light.Compiler.Framed, Light.Compiler.Rel.same, Light.Compiler.codeAt_after_pair, Light.Compiler.compileCond, Light.Compiler.inRange_sub, Light.Compiler.steps_pair, Light.Cond.Safe, Light.Cond.size, Light.Cond.width, Light.Cond.width_lt_le_iff, Light.Expr.abs_val_le, Light.Expr.val, Light.State.Bounded, WordRAM.AgreeOutside.update, WordRAM.CodeAt, WordRAM.CodeAt.tail, WordRAM.Steps.branch, WordRAM.Steps.trans, WordRAM.steps_bltz, WordRAM.steps_sub}
\difficulty{5}
Let $Z$ be a compiler layout with frame width $F$, dispatcher position $D$, limits
$(w,S)$, and stack capacity $Q$, satisfying $2(2w+2)<2^W$, $2S<2^W$, $4Q<2^W$, $2D<2^W$,
and $2(F+1)\le D$. Let $\sigma$ be a light-program state, $q$ a stack position, and $m$
a word-RAM memory representing $\sigma$ in a frame at $q$: the designated constant cells
contain $1$, $0$, and $-1$; the pool cells through position $D$ contain their indices;
the frame pointer contains $-2q$; the frame cells encode the first $F$ locations of
$\sigma$; and the memory cells at addresses below $S$ encode the corresponding values of
$\sigma$. Suppose $1\le q$ and $q+F\le Q$, every location and memory value of $\sigma$
has absolute value at most $w$, the code beginning at position $pos$ has as a prefix the
compiled test of $a<b$ with target position $l$, the test's width is at most $F$, and
both expressions are safe under the limits in state $\sigma$. Then there are a final
memory $m'$ and a number of execution steps $n$ no greater than the test's size such
that, if $a$ evaluates to less than $b$ in $\sigma$, execution from position $pos$ and
memory $m$ reaches position $pos$ plus the test's size with memory $m'$; otherwise it
reaches position $l$ with memory $m'$. The final memory agrees with $m$ outside the
cells reserved for scratch values: the difference, return, return-register, and
next-frame-pointer cells, the address cell, and temporary cells indexed from $0$ through
$2F$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Compiled equality test]
\lean{Light.Compiler.decides_eq}
\label{Light.Compiler.decides_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.Decides, Light.Compiler.Framed, Light.Compiler.Rel.same, Light.Compiler.cD, Light.Compiler.codeAt_after_pair, Light.Compiler.compileCond, Light.Compiler.inRange_sub, Light.Compiler.steps_pair, Light.Cond.Safe, Light.Cond.size, Light.Cond.width, Light.Cond.width_eq_le_iff, Light.Expr.abs_val_le, Light.Expr.val, Light.State.Bounded, WordRAM.AgreeOutside.update, WordRAM.CodeAt, WordRAM.CodeAt.tail, WordRAM.Steps.branch, WordRAM.Steps.trans, WordRAM.steps_bltz, WordRAM.steps_sub, WordRAM.wd}
\difficulty{5}
Let $Z$ be compiler size data for word size $W$, with local-frame capacity $Z.F$, limits
$Z.lim$, stack capacity $Z.Q$, and a memory layout and code layout as specified by $Z$.
Let $\sigma$ be a light state and let $q$ be a stack position such that memory $m$
represents $\sigma$ in a frame at $q$, with $1 \le q$ and $q+Z.F \le Z.Q$. Suppose
every location and memory value of $\sigma$ has absolute value at most $Z.lim.word$,
the code beginning at position $pos$ contains the compiled equality test for expressions
$a,b$ with target position $l$, this condition has width at most $Z.F$, and both
expressions are safe under $Z.lim$ in $\sigma$. Then there is a final memory $m'$
and a number of steps $n$ no greater than the size of the equality condition such that
execution from $pos$ reaches $pos$ plus that size if $a$ and $b$ have equal values in
$\sigma$, and reaches $l$ otherwise; throughout this execution, memory agrees with
$m$ outside the scratch cells for a frame of size $Z.F$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness of compiled conditions]
\lean{Light.Compiler.decides_compileCond}
\label{Light.Compiler.decides_compileCond}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.Decides, Light.Compiler.Framed, Light.Compiler.compileCond, Light.Compiler.decides_eq, Light.Compiler.decides_lt, Light.Cond, Light.Cond.Holds, Light.Cond.Safe, Light.Cond.size, Light.Cond.width, Light.State.Bounded, WordRAM.CodeAt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $W$ be a word width, let $Z$ be a compiler size record with local-variable bound $F$
and stack bound $Q$, and let $\sigma$ be a program state represented by a
word-RAM memory $m$ in a frame at stack position $q$. Suppose the frame representation
stores the designated words $1$, $0$, and $-1$ at their respective addresses, stores
each pool index $n$ up to the dispatcher position at its pool address, stores the frame
pointer at the stack address for $q$, and stores each local value and memory value at
the corresponding stack address and memory address within their specified bounds; also
suppose $1\le q$, $q+F\le Q$, and every value of the state has absolute value at most
the word bound. If a condition $c$ has width at most $F$, is safe for the resource
limits and state, and its compiled code occurs at position $pos$ in a program, then
there are a memory $m'$ and a number $n\le\mathrm{size}(c)$ such that $m'$ agrees with
$m$ outside the scratch and temporary addresses for $F$ local variables. Execution from
$pos$ reaches $pos+\mathrm{size}(c)$ in $n$ steps when $c$ holds, and reaches the
specified target position $l$ in $n$ steps when $c$ does not hold, with the same
resulting memory $m'$.
\end{theorem}
